items.note: Within-subjects study in which participants did the Alternative Uses Task with flexible AI, persistent AI, or no AI, with originality scored; condition order randomization not stated and N=35 is below the 50-person threshold.

Mixed-methods experiment with 41 product-design students comparing unaided, Internet-assisted, and GenAI-assisted ideation on divergent-thinking performance of design outcomes plus perceived creativity support; design (within or between) and assignment not stated, and N is below 50.

Single-factor between-subjects experiment with 113 college students using Kimi AI as a learning companion, with creativity scored on an alien-drawing divergent-thinking task; random assignment and the comparison condition are not described in the abstract.

Quasi-experiment with 230 Chinese university students in human-ChatGPT, human-Google, and human-human groups on a mathematical creativity task scored for fluency, flexibility, and originality; non-random assignment (quasi-experiment), so likely observational context if assignment is confirmed non-random.

Five-day between-subjects classroom study with 38 children aged 7-11 comparing an analogical curriculum with and without an LLM agent (AHAlogy), with divergent thinking (fluency, flexibility, originality) scored; assignment method not stated and N is below 50; extended abstract.

Experiment with 78 primary school students assigned to GenAI-supported writing (n=20), peer collaboration (n=38, 19 pairs), or individual writing (n=20), with creative writing performance scored; abstract says assigned but not how, and only 40 students are in the GenAI versus individual comparison.

Systematic review of 27 empirical and theoretical studies (January 2022 to March 2024) on generative AI tools and creativity in education, focused on art and design; no meta-analytic pooled estimate mentioned.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect, web search all failed); from the title, likely a firm-level study of generative AI and innovation quantity versus quality (probably patents), so the next stage should confirm it has a novelty or originality outcome rather than only patent counts.

Randomized experiment (N=486) comparing human-led reflective and model-led LLM co-creation modes on idea quality, idea diversity, and perceived ownership, replicated in a second context (N=640); search notes say a no-AI arm exists, which the abstract does not mention; same study as arXiv 2510.23324.

Pre-registered before-and-after analysis of 4,820 empirical reports by 2,000 psychology undergraduates (2016-2025) around ChatGPT's release, measuring style (including lexical diversity), sentiment, grades, and similarity to GPT text; borderline, since it has no across-writer diversity or creativity outcome and may fall under the AI-text-prevalence exclusion.
